column2: What it means in an interview
Foundation. Fair game from an internship interview onward  and still expected at 3 YOE. Fumbling these ends a loop regardless of your years.
Applied professional level. This is the bulk of your interviews right now.
Senior-leaning. Not required at 3 YOE  but a demanding panel may probe it as a ceiling test.
Lead / staff scope. Not a prerequisite for any role you are targeting today.
Depends on the job description  not on tenure. A Vue beginner topic is still a beginner topic.
What the interviewer is testing
Implement it independently  with API documentation open. You do not need to recite the signature.
Build it  explain how it executes  diagnose a broken example  and argue the tradeoffs. The gotcha rows.
Explain it accurately and say when you would reach for it. Implementing its internals is unnecessary.
How often it actually comes up
Asked in most interviews at that level. Non-negotiable.
Comes up regularly. Expect it in roughly half your loops.
Occasional. A differentiator  not a gate.

column2: Target: score 3 on every B row  4 on every D row  and an accurate one-paragraph answer on every E row. You do not need a 4 on everything to start applying.
Work down Core Syllabus in order. The sheet is already sorted HTML → CSS → JavaScript → TypeScript → React → production.
Set Status from the dropdown in column I. Score fills itself from the table above  and the Dashboard updates.
Filter column G to Core when you are short on time. Those rows are the ones that decide most interviews.
Filter column F to D to drill the gotcha rows — the ones where an interviewer follows up with 'why?'.
Ignore Advanced Web until you have an offer. It is a roadmap  not a gate.
Open Role Branches only when a job description names that stack  then treat that branch as core for that application.
Column K is yours. Put the link to the exercise you solved  or the thing you got wrong  so revision has something to bite on.

Every YOE label is an editorial preparation estimate. Neither platform publishes a concept-by-concept YOE scale  and no hiring data was measured. A label is not a promise that a topic cannot be asked earlier — demanding panels ask graph and DP questions of graduates.

The catalogue review was thorough at concept level: the full lesson trees of ~45 Master.dev courses via its course API  and Scrimba's complete career-path lesson list decoded from its path data. It is not a certified transcription of every video in either subscription.
Depth codes (B/D/E) are defaults derived from how each row behaves in an interview  then hand-checked on the high-value rows. Disagree with one and change it — that is what column F is for.
Frontend Masters rebranded to Master.dev during this research; frontendmasters.com redirects there. Course titles are as observed on 20 September 2026.
Version-sensitive areas — React 19  Next.js caching  Angular signals  Svelte runes — age fast. Check the installed version's docs before copying any API from a tutorial.
A course named 'Advanced React' can contain ordinary hireable skills. Scrimba's includes routing  performance and auth. Do not defer a whole course because of its title.
